payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the Way; the Name that can be named is not the Name; the Nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth, the Name is the mother of all things. The constant absence of desire allows one to see the wonderful; the constant desire allows one to see the boundary. These two are of the same origin but different names. They are called the Void. The Void is again and again the Void. The Gate of the Many Mysteries.

issues.span: the Name is the mother of all things
issues.advice: Source is 有名萬物之母 — 'the named' (having names), not 'the Name'; render as 'the named is the mother of all things' to preserve the 無名/有名 contrast.

issues.span: The constant absence of desire allows one to see the wonderful; the constant desire allows one to see the boundary
issues.advice: Source 常無欲/常有欲 — 'constantly without desire' / 'constantly with desire'; the translation shifts 常 to modify 'absence/desire' rather than the state, and 'the wonderful'/'the boundary' should reflect 妙 (subtlety/wonder) and 徼 (outward manifestations/boundaries).

issues.span: They are called the Void. The Void is again and again the Void.
issues.advice: 玄 is conventionally 'mystery'/'darkness', not 'Void'; and 同謂之玄 means 'both are called mystery', while 玄之又玄 is 'mystery upon mystery'. 'Void' mistranslates the key term and the repetition structure.

issues.span: The Gate of the Many Mysteries.
issues.advice: 衆妙之門 is 'the gate of all wonders/marvels'; 'Many Mysteries' is imprecise and the sentence fragment should be integrated.

issues.span: The Void is again and again the Void. The Gate of the Many Mysteries.
issues.advice: Sentence fragments and awkward repetition reduce fluency; render as a coherent clause.

payload.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the Way; the Name that can be named is not the Name; the Nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth, while the Named is the mother of all things. Constant absence of desire allows one to see the wonderful; constant presence of desire allows one to see the boundary. These two are of the same origin but different names; they are both called the Void. The Void is mystery upon mystery. The Gate of the Many Mysteries.

issues.span: they are both called the Void
issues.advice: 玄 (xuan) is conventionally rendered 'mystery' or 'darkness', not 'Void'; 'Void' (空/kong) is a different concept. Render 同謂之玄 as 'both are called mystery/darkness'.

issues.span: The Void is mystery upon mystery. The Gate of the Many Mysteries.
issues.advice: The final clause 衆妙之門 is a predicate of 玄之又玄 ('mystery upon mystery—the gate of all wonders'); the translation splits it into a fragment. Join into one sentence: 'mystery upon mystery—the gate of all wonders.'

issues.span: the wonderful
issues.advice: 妙 (miao) is better rendered 'wonder' or 'subtlety'; 'the wonderful' as a bare adjective is awkward and non-standard.

issues.span: the boundary
issues.advice: 徼 (jiao) is conventionally 'manifestation', 'outward form', or 'boundary/appearance'; 'boundary' alone is acceptable but 'manifestation' better contrasts with 妙.

issues.span: The Gate of the Many Mysteries.
issues.advice: Sentence fragment; integrate with preceding clause or make a complete sentence.

payload.translation: Le savoir peut être dit, et ce qui est dit n'est pas le même savoir; le nom peut être nommé, et ce qui est nommé n'est pas le même nom. Le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses et la mère des choses; le nom a des choses. Il faut souvent se désintéresser pour observer la subtilité, et souvent se désintéresser pour observer les limites. Ces deux sont d'une seule origine mais ont des noms différents. On les appelle le Sombre. Le Sombre est encore le Sombre. La porte des choses infiniment subtiles.

issues.span: Le savoir peut être dit
issues.advice: 道 here is the Way, not 'savoir/knowledge'; render as 'La Voie' to preserve the Daoist concept.

issues.span: et ce qui est dit n'est pas le même savoir
issues.advice: The negation 非常道 means 'is not the constant/eternal Way', not 'not the same knowledge'; convey 常 as 'constant/éternel'.

issues.span: le nom peut être nommé, et ce qui est nommé n'est pas le même nom
issues.advice: Again 常名 = 'the constant name'; the clause should negate constancy, not identity.

issues.span: Le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses et la mère des choses; le nom a des choses.
issues.advice: The structure is 無名天地之始 / 有名萬物之母: 'the nameless is the origin of heaven and earth; the named is the mother of the ten thousand things.' The current rendering merges and distorts this, and 'le nom a des choses' is a mistranslation.

issues.span: Il faut souvent se désintéresser pour observer la subtilité, et souvent se désintéresser pour observer les limites
issues.advice: The contrast is 常無欲 (constant freedom from desire) vs 常有欲 (constant having desire); the second clause should express 'having desire' to observe the manifestations, not repeat 'se désintéresser'.

issues.span: Le Sombre est encore le Sombre
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 means 'darkness within darkness' / 'mystery upon mystery', not a flat repetition; render the intensification.

issues.span: La porte des choses infiniment subtiles
issues.advice: 衆妙之門 = 'the gate of all wonders/marvels'; 'choses infiniment subtiles' misreads 妙.

issues.span: le Sombre
issues.advice: 玄 is conventionally rendered 'le Mystère' or 'l'Obscur' in French Daoist translations; 'Sombre' is non-standard and loses the metaphysical sense.

issues.span: le nom a des choses
issues.advice: This fragment is ungrammatical and unclear in French; the clause needs a coherent predicate.

issues.span: Le savoir peut être dit
issues.advice: Rendering 道 as 'savoir' removes the foundational Daoist term; use 'la Voie' to preserve cultural reference.

payload.translation: La Voie peut être dite, et ce qui est dit n'est pas la même Voie ; le nom peut être nommé, et ce qui est nommé n'est pas le même nom. Le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses et la mère des choses ; le nom a des choses. Il faut souvent se désintéresser pour observer la subtilité, et souvent se désintéresser pour observer les manifestations. Ces deux sont d'une seule origine mais ont des noms différents. On les appelle le Mystère. Le Mystère est encore le Mystère. La porte des choses infiniment subtiles.

issues.span: Le nom sans nom est le commencement des choses et la mère des choses ; le nom a des choses.
issues.advice: The source distinguishes 無名 (the nameless) as the beginning of heaven and earth (天地之始) and 有名 (the named) as the mother of the ten thousand things (萬物之母). The translation collapses both into 'des choses' and renders 有名 as the nonsensical 'le nom a des choses'. Restore the contrast: the nameless = beginning of heaven and earth; the named = mother of the myriad things.

issues.span: et souvent se désintéresser pour observer les manifestations
issues.advice: The source reads 常有欲以觀其徼 (constantly having desire to observe its manifestations/boundaries). The translation repeats 'se désintéresser' (to be disinterested) for both clauses, inverting the second clause's meaning. Render the second as 'avoir des désirs' / 'être dans le désir'.

issues.span: Le Mystère est encore le Mystère.
issues.advice: 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery' / 'mystery of mysteries', not a flat repetition. Convey the intensification.

issues.span: La porte des choses infiniment subtiles.
issues.advice: 衆妙之門 is 'the gate of all wonders/marvels'. 'choses infiniment subtiles' mistranslates 妙 (wonder/marvel) and drops the gate-of-all-wonders sense; also it is a fragment lacking a verb connecting to the preceding sentence.

issues.span: La Voie peut être dite, et ce qui est dit n'est pas la même Voie
issues.advice: 道 as the key term is conventionally rendered 'la Voie' (acceptable), but the gloss 'ce qui est dite' vs 'la même Voie' loses the wordplay 道/可道 (the Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way). Consider preserving the constant/eternal (常) sense: 'la Voie qui peut être énoncée n'est pas la Voie éternelle'.

issues.span: le nom peut être nommé, et ce qui est nommé n'est pas le même nom
issues.advice: 常名 (the constant/eternal name) is dropped; render as 'le nom qui peut être nommé n'est pas le Nom éternel' to preserve the parallel with 常道.

issues.span: Ces deux sont d'une seule origine mais ont des noms différents.
issues.advice: Acceptable, but 'Ces deux' lacks a clear antecedent and the sentence flow is choppy; ensure the two (nameless/named, or desire/no-desire) are clearly referenced.

payload.translation: 道は言及せず、道は非道である。名は言及せず、名は非名である。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物的母である。常無を欲せず、妙を観ず。常欲を欲せず、徼を観ず。これら二つは同一の源から出ているが異名である。これを玄と呼ぶ。玄は玄であり、玄之又玄。衆妙の門である。

issues.span: 道は言及せず、道は非道である
issues.advice: The source says '道可道非常道' (the Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao). The translation reverses the meaning: it says 'do not speak of the Dao, the Dao is non-Dao.' Render the conditional sense: '道は道うべきものなれど、常の道にあらず' or similar.

issues.span: 名は言及せず、名は非名である
issues.advice: Same error as above: '名可名非常名' means 'the name that can be named is not the constant name,' not 'do not mention the name.'

issues.span: 常無を欲せず、妙を観ず
issues.advice: Source '常無欲以觀其妙' means 'constantly without desire, thereby observe its wonder.' The translation negates the wrong element ('do not desire the constant non-being'). Render as '常に無欲にして以てその妙を観る.'

issues.span: 常欲を欲せず、徼を観ず
issues.advice: Source '常有欲以觀其徼' means 'constantly having desire, thereby observe its manifestations.' The translation again negates incorrectly. Render as '常に欲ありて以てその徼を観る.'

issues.span: 万物的母
issues.advice: '万物的母' is not idiomatic Japanese; use '万物の母' (or '万物の母である').

issues.span: 玄之又玄
issues.advice: Leaving the Chinese phrase untranslated breaks the Japanese flow; render as '玄の又玄' or '玄にして又玄'.

issues.span: これら二つは同一の源から出ているが異名である
issues.advice: Acceptable but stiff; '同じく出でて名を異にする' better matches the classical register.

issues.span: 道は言及せず
issues.advice: The register is modern explanatory prose rather than the classical Japanese style appropriate for the Daodejing; consider a classical/literary register (e.g., '道うべき道は常の道にあらず').

payload.translation: 道は言及せず、道は常の道にあらず。名は言及せず、名は常の名にあらず。無名は天地の始まり、有名は万物の母なり。常無を欲せず、妙を観ず。常欲を欲せず、徼を観ず。これら二つは同一の源から出でて名を異にする。これを玄と呼び、玄にして又玄。衆妙の門なり。

issues.span: 道は言及せず、道は常の道にあらず
issues.advice: The source 道可道非常道 means 'the Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way'; the translation adds '言及せず' (does not mention) and splits the clause incorrectly, losing the conditional 'can be spoken' structure.

issues.span: 名は言及せず、名は常の名にあらず
issues.advice: Similarly 名可名非常名 means 'the name that can be named is not the constant name'; the added '言及せず' is not in the source and the structure is misrendered.

issues.span: 常無を欲せず、妙を観ず。常欲を欲せず、徼を観ず
issues.advice: The source 常無欲以觀其妙 / 常有欲以觀其徼 means 'constantly without desire, thereby observe its subtlety; constantly with desire, thereby observe its manifestations.' The translation negates 欲 ('常無を欲せず' = 'does not desire constant non-being') and inverts the meaning; 欲 should be read as 'desire' modifying the observer, not negated.

issues.span: 玄
issues.advice: 玄 is a key Daoist term (mystery/darkness); rendering it as 玄 in katakana-free kanji is acceptable but should be consistently treated as a technical term, e.g., 玄（神秘）; the current handling is inconsistent with the philosophical register.

issues.span: 玄にして又玄
issues.advice: The phrase 玄之又玄 means 'mystery upon mystery'; '玄にして又玄' is awkward and unclear in Japanese; a smoother rendering such as 玄のまた玄 would read better.

payload.translation: The highest virtue is like water; water benefits all things without striving. It dwells where others find no place, is good at the deep, and is kind to all. It speaks truthfully and acts with sincerity. It governs affairs wisely and can move with timing. It is because it does not strive.

issues.span: It dwells where others find no place
issues.advice: The source 處衆人之所惡 means 'dwells in places that people despise/loathe,' not 'where others find no place.' Render the sense of 惡 as 'despise/dislike.'

issues.span: is good at the deep
issues.advice: 心善淵 means the heart/mind is good at (or inclined toward) depth/profundity; 'is good at the deep' is awkward and loses the 心 (heart/mind) subject. Convey 'its heart is good at depth.'

issues.span: and is kind to all
issues.advice: 與善仁 means 'in association/relationships it is good at benevolence' (與 = in dealings with others), not 'kind to all.' Reflect the 與 (association) sense.

issues.span: It speaks truthfully and acts with sincerity
issues.advice: 言善信 is 'in speech it is good at trustworthiness'; 'acts with sincerity' adds content not in the source. Keep the speech/trustworthiness pairing.

issues.span: It governs affairs wisely and can move with timing
issues.advice: 政善治 and 事善能 and 動善時 are three distinct clauses: governance good at ordering, affairs good at competence, movement good at timing. The translation merges/omits 事善能 and blurs 政善治.

issues.span: It is because it does not strive.
issues.advice: The source 夫惟不爭 is an incomplete clause leading into the next line (故無尤); as rendered it is a dangling fragment. Render the causal sense 'It is precisely because it does not strive...' and note the sentence is truncated.

issues.span: The highest virtue
issues.advice: 上善 is conventionally rendered 'the highest good' in Daodejing translations; 'highest virtue' conflates 善 with 德. Consider 'the highest good.'

issues.span: without striving
issues.advice: 不爭 is a key Daoist term often rendered 'without contention/striving'; acceptable, but ensure consistency with the final 不爭 clause.

payload.translation: The highest good is like water; water benefits all things without striving. It dwells in places that people despise, is good at the deep, and is kind in associations. It speaks truthfully and acts with sincerity. It governs affairs wisely, handles matters competently, and moves with timing. It is precisely because it does not strive.

issues.span: It dwells in places that people despise, is good at the deep, and is kind in associations.
issues.advice: The source lists seven parallel '善' phrases (居善地, 心善淵, 與善仁, 言善信, 政善治, 事善能, 動善時). The translation merges and misaligns them: '心善淵' is rendered as 'is good at the deep' rather than the heart/mind being good at depth; '與善仁' is rendered as 'kind in associations' rather than being good in giving/association with benevolence. Keep each clause distinct and parallel.

issues.span: It speaks truthfully and acts with sincerity.
issues.advice: '言善信' means words are good at being trustworthy/faithful; 'acts with sincerity' is not present in the source and should be removed or replaced with the correct clause.

issues.span: It governs affairs wisely, handles matters competently, and moves with timing.
issues.advice: '政善治' refers to governance being good at order/administration; 'governs affairs wisely' blurs 政 (government) with 事 (affairs). Render 政善治 as governing well/orderly governance, and 事善能 as affairs being handled capably.

issues.span: It is precisely because it does not strive.
issues.advice: The source ends with '夫惟不爭' (only because it does not contend), which is an incomplete clause leading into the omitted conclusion (故無尤). The translation presents it as a complete sentence, losing the causal 'because... therefore' structure and the sense of 夫惟.

issues.span: without striving
issues.advice: '不爭' is conventionally rendered 'does not contend/compete'; 'striving' is acceptable but should be consistent with the final '夫惟不爭' clause, which is translated as 'does not strive' — keep the term consistent.

issues.span: The highest good is like water
issues.advice: This is a standard rendering of 上善若水 and is acceptable, but the passage is from the Dao De Jing (Ch. 8); consider noting the water metaphor's Daoist framing of 善 as efficacy rather than moral goodness, to avoid reading 'good' purely ethically.

payload.translation: Le plus haut bien est comme l'eau ; l'eau est utile à tous les êtres sans se battre. Elle habite là où les autres désirent le mal, et elle est proche du Dao. Elle habite le bon lieu, le bon fond, et le bon cœur, parlant avec le bon sens et la bonne foi. Elle gouverne le bien et fait le bien. Elle sait agir au bon moment. C'est parce qu'elle ne se bat pas.

issues.span: Elle habite là où les autres désirent le mal
issues.advice: 處衆人之所惡 means 'dwells in places that people despise/dislike', not 'where others desire evil'. Render as 'là où les gens ne veulent pas habiter' or 'dans les lieux que les gens dédaignent'.

issues.span: Elle habite le bon lieu, le bon fond, et le bon cœur
issues.advice: 居善地心善淵與善仁 is a series of parallel phrases: 'demeure dans un bon lieu, son cœur est un abîme (de profondeur) bon, dans ses relations il est bon/bienveillant'. The translation collapses 心善淵 and 與善仁 into 'bon fond' and 'bon cœur', losing the distinct meanings of 淵 (abyss/depth) and 與 (relations/association).

issues.span: Elle gouverne le bien et fait le bien
issues.advice: 政善治事善能: 'dans le gouvernement, il sait bien administrer; dans les affaires, il sait être efficace/capable'. The translation reduces both to vague 'le bien' and omits 事善能 (efficiency in affairs).

issues.span: C'est parce qu'elle ne se bat pas.
issues.advice: The final clause 夫惟不爭 is incomplete in the source excerpt but the translation ends abruptly; it should convey 'C'est justement parce qu'il ne lutte pas (qu'il ne peut être critiqué)' — at minimum render the causal link clearly rather than a dangling sentence.

issues.span: sans se battre
issues.advice: 不爭 in Daoist context is better rendered 'sans lutter' or 'sans rivaliser' rather than 'se battre' (physical fighting).

issues.span: le Dao
issues.advice: Acceptable, but consider 'la Voie' as the standard French rendering of 道 in Laozi translations.

issues.span: Elle habite le bon lieu, le bon fond, et le bon cœur, parlant avec le bon sens et la bonne foi.
issues.advice: The repetition of 'bon' is awkward and the parallel structure of the original is lost; restructure to reflect the seven parallel clauses.

payload.translation: Le plus haut bien est comme l'eau ; l'eau est utile à tous les êtres sans se battre. Elle habite là où les gens ne veulent pas habiter, et elle est proche de la Voie. Elle demeure dans un bon lieu, son cœur est un abîme profond, et ses relations sont d'une bonté et d'une association. Elle parle avec le bon sens et la bonne foi. Elle gouverne le bien et fait le bien. Elle sait agir au bon moment. C'est justement parce qu'elle ne se bat pas.

issues.span: et ses relations sont d'une bonté et d'une association
issues.advice: 與善仁 means 'in association/giving, it is good in benevolence (ren)'. The rendering 'bonté et d'une association' misparses 與 (association) as a separate noun and splits 善仁; render as 'dans ses relations, elle est bienveillante'.

issues.span: Elle parle avec le bon sens et la bonne foi
issues.advice: 言善信 = 'in speech, it is good in trustworthiness/sincerity'. 'bon sens' (good sense) is not 信; use 'fidèle à sa parole' or 'sincère'.

issues.span: Elle gouverne le bien et fait le bien
issues.advice: 政善治事善能 = 'in governing, it is good at ordering; in affairs, it is good at ability'. The translation collapses two distinct clauses and loses 事善能; render 'dans le gouvernement, elle sait bien ordonner; dans les affaires, elle est capable'.

issues.span: C'est justement parce qu'elle ne se bat pas.
issues.advice: The source ends 夫惟不爭 (only because it does not contend...), an incomplete clause; the French sentence is also incomplete but drops the causal 'parce que' structure's consequence. Keep as 'C'est justement parce qu'elle ne se bat pas...' preserving the open ending, or note the ellipsis.

issues.span: la Voie
issues.advice: 道 in Daodejing is conventionally rendered 'la Voie' (acceptable), but ensure consistency; fine.

issues.span: Elle habite là où les gens ne veux pas habiter
issues.advice: Grammar error: 'les gens ne veulent pas'. Also 處衆人之所惡 = 'dwells in what people detest'; 'là où les gens ne veulent pas habiter' is acceptable but 'ce que les gens détestent' is closer.

issues.span: son cœur est un abîme profond
issues.advice: 心善淵 = 'in heart, it is good at depth'; 'abîme profond' is a reasonable rendering but 'son cœur est profond comme un abîme' flows better.

payload.translation: 上善如水，水善利万物而不争，处众人之所恶，故几于道。居善地，心善渊，与善仁，言善信，政善治，事善能，动善时。夫惟不争。

issues.span: 夫惟不争。
issues.advice: The final clause is left incomplete; the source continues (夫惟不争，故无尤). Either complete the sentence or mark the truncation so the fragment does not read as a full stop.

issues.span: 上善如水
issues.advice: Classical Chinese text rendered in simplified characters; if the target audience expects Japanese kanji rendering, consider whether character forms match the intended register.

payload.translation: Carrying wealth to excess is not as good as having it at hand; sharpening it is not as secure as keeping it; gold and jade are filled with treasures, yet no one can guard them; to be rich and proud is to lose one's own fault; when merit and fame are achieved, one retires. This is the way of heaven.

issues.span: Carrying wealth to excess is not as good as having it at hand
issues.advice: The source 持而盈之 means 'to hold and fill to overflowing'; it does not mention wealth. Render as holding/filling to excess, not 'carrying wealth'.

issues.span: sharpening it is not as secure as keeping it
issues.advice: 揣而銳之 means 'to hammer/shape and sharpen it'; 不可長保 means 'cannot be preserved for long'. The translation reverses the sense ('not as secure as keeping it').

issues.span: gold and jade are filled with treasures
issues.advice: 金玉滿堂 means 'gold and jade fill the hall'; the translation misassigns 'filled with treasures' to the gold and jade rather than the hall.

issues.span: to be rich and proud is to lose one's own fault
issues.advice: 自遺其咎 means 'to bring disaster/calamity upon oneself', not 'to lose one's own fault'. Reverse the meaning.

issues.span: when merit and fame are achieved, one retires
issues.advice: Acceptable in sense, but 身退 means 'withdraw the self/retire from position'; fine, though 'retire' alone is slightly narrow.

issues.span: This is the way of heaven
issues.advice: 天之道 is conventionally 'the Way of Heaven'; capitalize 'Way' to match standard Daoist terminology.

payload.translation: Holding and filling to overflowing is not as good as having it at hand; hammering and sharpening it is not as secure as keeping it; gold and jade fill the hall, yet no one can guard them; to be rich and proud is to bring disaster upon oneself; when merit and fame are achieved, one withdraws from office. This is the Way of Heaven.

issues.span: is not as good as having it at hand
issues.advice: The source 不如其已 means 'it is better to stop/cease', not 'having it at hand'. Render as 'is not as good as stopping'.

issues.span: is not as secure as keeping it
issues.advice: The source 不可長保 means 'cannot be preserved for long', not a comparison with 'keeping it'. Render as 'cannot be preserved for long'.

issues.span: to be rich and proud is to bring disaster upon oneself
issues.advice: The source 自遺其咎 means 'brings blame/calamity upon oneself' — acceptable, but 'disaster' overstates; consider 'brings ruin/blame upon oneself'.

issues.span: withdraws from office
issues.advice: 身退 in the Daodejing context means 'withdraw oneself / retire from the position', not merely 'withdraw from office'; render as 'one withdraws (retires) oneself'.

issues.span: Holding and filling to overflowing
issues.advice: The parallel structure of 持而盈之 / 揣而銳之 is lost; keep parallel phrasing such as 'Rather than fill it to the brim by holding it...'.

payload.translation: Levantant-leur, ils ne sont pas aussi riches que lorsqu'ils les ont; les aiguillons, on ne peut pas les prolonger; les or et l'argent ne peuvent pas être gardés dans un lieu rempli de richesses; on ne peut pas garder ses richesses et sa gloire; on se fait honneur et on se fait orgueil, et on se fait sa propre faute; le succès de ses mérites et de ses gloires, et la retraite de son corps, c'est la voie du ciel.

issues.span: Levantant-leur, ils ne sont pas aussi riches que lorsqu'ils les ont
issues.advice: The source 持而盈之不如其已 means 'to hold and fill it to overflowing is not as good as stopping in time'; the translation invents 'riche' and misreads 盈之 (filling it) and 已 (stopping). Render the sense of holding/filling versus desisting.

issues.span: les aiguillons, on ne peut pas les prolonger
issues.advice: 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'to hammer and sharpen it to a point cannot be kept long'; 'aiguillons' (stings) is a mistranslation of 銳 (sharp/pointed), and 長保 is 'long preserved', not 'prolonged'.

issues.span: les or et l'argent ne peuvent pas être gardés dans un lieu rempli de richesses
issues.advice: 金玉滿堂莫之能守 means 'gold and jade fill the hall, yet none can guard them'; the translation reverses the logic (riches cannot be kept in a place full of riches) and mistranslates 金玉 as 'or et argent'.

issues.span: on ne peut pas garder ses richesses et sa gloire
issues.advice: 富貴而驕自遺其咎 means 'wealth and honor with arrogance bring self-inflicted blame'; the translation drops 驕 (arrogance) and misassigns the clause.

issues.span: on se fait honneur et on se fait orgueil, et on se fait sa propre faute
issues.advice: This duplicates and garbles the previous clause; 自遺其咎 is 'one brings blame upon oneself', not 'se fait honneur'.

issues.span: le succès de ses mérites et de ses gloires, et la retraite de son corps, c'est la voie du ciel
issues.advice: 功成名遂身退天之道 means 'when the work is accomplished and fame achieved, to withdraw the self is the Way of Heaven'; 'retraite de son corps' is a literal mistranslation of 身退 (withdraw oneself).

issues.span: la voie du ciel

issues.span: Levantant-leur
issues.advice: Non-word ('levant' is the correct participle); the whole sentence is ungrammatical and needs restructuring.

issues.span: les or et l'argent
issues.advice: Incorrect article/plural agreement; 'or' is invariable and should be 'l'or et l'argent'.

payload.translation: Leur emplit et ne l'est plus comme il l'était; leur pointe ne peut être conservée longtemps; l'or et l'argent ne peuvent être gardés dans un lieu rempli de richesses; on ne peut pas garder ses richesses et sa gloire; on se fait honneur et on se fait orgueil, et on se fait sa propre faute; le succès de ses mérites et de ses gloires, et la retraite de son corps, c'est la Voie du Ciel.

payload.translation: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず、揣て鋭くは長きものなり、金玉を満たてて守るべからず、富貴を誇りしむれば咎を遺すなり、功を遂げて身を退くべし、天の道なり。

issues.span: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず
issues.advice: The source says 不如其已 ('better to stop/desist'), not 止むを得ず ('cannot help but'). Render the comparative sense: holding and overfilling is not as good as stopping.

issues.span: 揣て鋭くは長きものなり
issues.advice: Source is 不可長保 ('cannot be preserved for long'), a negative. The translation asserts it is long-lasting, reversing the meaning. Express the impossibility of long preservation.

issues.span: 金玉を満たてて守るべからず
issues.advice: Source 莫之能守 means 'no one can keep them'; 守るべからず is a prohibition ('must not keep'), which is wrong modality. Use a potential-negative: cannot be guarded/kept.

issues.span: 富貴を誇りしむれば咎を遺すなり
issues.advice: Source 富貴而驕自遺其咎: wealth and honor plus arrogance brings self-inflicted blame. '誇りしむれば' is causative/odd; render 'being arrogant amid wealth and honor leaves oneself blame.'

issues.span: 功を遂げて身を退くべし
issues.advice: Source 功成名遂身退 is descriptive of the way of heaven, not an imperative 'べし'. Render as 'when merit is accomplished and name achieved, to withdraw the self—this is the way of heaven.'

issues.span: 揣て
issues.advice: '揣て' is not a natural Japanese form; use 揣(はか)って or a clearer rendering of 'hammering/sharpening to a point.'

issues.span: 天の道なり
issues.advice: Classical 天之道 is conventionally rendered 天の道; acceptable, but ensure the preceding clause is not imperative so the identification with 天の道 reads correctly.

payload.translation: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず、揣て鋭くは長きものなり、金玉を満たてて守るべからず、富貴を誇りしむれば咎を遺すなり、功を遂げて身を退くべし。天の道なり。

issues.span: 持ちて満ちては止むを得ず
issues.advice: The source 持而盈之不如其已 means 'to hold and overfill it is not as good as stopping'; the translation reverses the meaning (止むを得ず = 'unavoidably'). Render the comparative '不如其已' as '止むに如かず'.

issues.span: 揣て鋭くは長きものなり
issues.advice: Source 揣而銳之不可長保 means 'hammered sharp, it cannot be preserved long'; the translation says it IS long-lasting, inverting the negation 不可長保.

issues.span: 金玉を満たてて守るべからず
issues.advice: Source 金玉滿堂莫之能守 means 'gold and jade fill the hall, none can guard them'; the translation turns it into a prohibition ('must not guard') rather than an inability.

issues.span: 富貴を誇りしむれば咎を遺すなり
issues.advice: Source 富貴而驕自遺其咎 means 'wealth and honor with arrogance brings guilt upon oneself'; 自遺其咎 is self-inflicted, not merely 'leaves guilt'. Also 誇りしむ is not idiomatic.

issues.span: 功を遂げて身を退くべし
issues.advice: Source 功成名遂身退 is descriptive of the way of heaven ('when work is done and name achieved, retire the body'); べし turns it into an imperative, and 名遂 (name achieved) is omitted.

issues.span: 揣て鋭くは長きものなり
issues.advice: Classical 揣 (to hammer/beat) is misread; the clause is ungrammatical and the connective は is wrong. Use a conditional or concessive structure.

issues.span: 持ちて満ちては
issues.advice: Classical 持而盈之 is a parallel construction; 持ちて満ちては loses the object 之 and the 而 linkage. Render as '持して之を盈たすは'.

issues.span: 天の道なり
issues.advice: The closing 天之道 is a summary maxim; the translation's punctuation attaches it loosely. Keep it as a concluding statement '是れ天の道なり'.

payload.translation: The wise in ancient times, who skillfully cultivate the way of the scholar, are subtle, mysterious, profound, and deep, beyond recognition. For it is precisely because they are beyond recognition that they are cultivated with care and grace, like a winter person crossing a river, as if they feared their four neighbors, standing like guests, scattered like mist, like ice about to melt, pure as the primitive state, vast as the wilderness, like the clear valley, all mixed with turbidity. Who can make turbidity still? Who can gradually clear it? Who can make it still and quiet? Who can make it slow and calm? Who can make it slow and long? The one who preserves this way does not desire fullness. For it is precisely because they do not desire fullness that they can endure without newness and remain unblemished.

issues.span: who skillfully cultivate the way of the scholar
issues.advice: The source describes ancient masters who were skilled in the Way (善為士者 = those skilled as masters/scholars of the Way), not people who 'cultivate the way of the scholar'; render the subject as the ancient masters skilled in the Way.

issues.span: they are cultivated with care and grace
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'one is forced to describe their appearance/portray them'; it does not mean the masters are 'cultivated with care and grace'. Render as a reluctant attempt to describe them.

issues.span: like a winter person crossing a river
issues.advice: 豫若冬涉川 means hesitant/cautious like one crossing a river in winter; 'winter person' is a mistranslation of the simile.

issues.span: scattered like mist
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 means yielding/dissolving like ice about to melt; 'scattered like mist' misreads the image and duplicates the ice simile that follows.

issues.span: like the clear valley
issues.advice: 曠兮其若谷 means open/vast like a valley; 'clear valley' adds 'clear' not in the source.

issues.span: all mixed with turbidity
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 means simple/undifferentiated like muddy water; 'all mixed with turbidity' misconstrues the simile.

issues.span: Who can make turbidity still? Who can gradually clear it? Who can make it still and quiet? Who can make it slow and calm? Who can make it slow and long?
issues.advice: The source has two rhetorical questions: who can, from turbidity, quiet it and gradually clear it; who can, from stillness, long activate it and gradually generate life. The translation fragments and repeats these into five questions, losing the 濁以靜之徐清 / 安以乆動之徐生 parallel structure.

issues.span: they can endure without newness and remain unblemished
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'thus they can be worn/old without needing to be newly completed' — i.e., they can endure decay without seeking renewal. 'Remain unblemished' is not in the source.

issues.span: the primitive state
issues.advice: 樸 is a key Daoist term usually rendered 'uncarved block' or 'simplicity'; 'primitive state' loses the technical sense.

issues.span: the way of the scholar
issues.advice: 道 here is the Dao/Way as a technical concept; 'the way of the scholar' misrenders 士 and weakens the term.

issues.span: subtle, mysterious, profound, and deep, beyond recognition
issues.advice: The chain of adjectives is awkward and 'beyond recognition' for 不可識 is misleading; smooth the list and render 不可識 as 'cannot be known/fathomed'.

issues.span: feared their four neighbors
issues.advice: 畏四鄰 evokes cautious deference to neighboring states/people; 'feared their four neighbors' is literal but reads oddly — consider 'as if wary of neighboring states'.

payload.translation: Ancient masters skilled in the Way were subtle, mysterious, profound, and deep, beyond recognition. For it is precisely because they are beyond recognition that they are cultivated with care and grace, like a hesitant person crossing a river in winter, as if wary of neighboring states, standing like guests, yielding like ice about to melt, pure as the uncarved block, vast as the wilderness, like the clear valley, all undifferentiated yet simple. Who can still turbidity? Who can gradually clear it? Who can make it still and quiet? Who can make it slow and calm? Who can make it slow and long? The one who preserves this Way does not desire fullness. For it is precisely because they do not desire fullness that they can endure without newness and remain unblemished.

issues.span: they are cultivated with care and grace
issues.advice: The source 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe their appearance'; the translation misreads 彊為之容 as cultivation rather than reluctant description.

issues.span: like a hesitant person crossing a river in winter
issues.advice: 豫若冬涉川 means 'cautious/hesitant as one crossing a river in winter'—the sense of 豫 (cautious, hesitant) is acceptable but should not be conflated with the following 猶若畏四鄰; keep the parallel structure of the four similes.

issues.span: like the clear valley
issues.advice: 曠兮其若谷 means 'open/vast like a valley', not 'clear valley'; 曠 conveys spaciousness/openness.

issues.span: all undifferentiated yet simple
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 means 'chaotic/murky like muddy water'; the rendering 'undifferentiated yet simple' does not match 濁 (turbid/muddy).

issues.span: Who can still turbidity? Who can gradually clear it? Who can make it still and quiet? Who can make it slow and calm? Who can make it slow and long?
issues.advice: The source 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生 has two rhetorical questions: 'Who can, from turbidity, quiet it and gradually clarify it? Who can, from stillness, long activate it and gradually generate life?' The translation splits into five questions and loses the 濁→靜→清 and 安→動→生 progression.

issues.span: they can endure without newness and remain unblemished
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'thus they can be worn/old without needing new completion'—i.e., they can remain imperfect/old rather than seeking renewal; 'remain unblemished' is not supported.

issues.span: the Way
issues.advice: Consistent rendering of 道 as 'the Way' is fine, but 士 as 'masters' should be 'scholars/gentlemen/practitioners' to reflect 士 rather than 師.

issues.span: Who can still turbidity?
issues.advice: Ungrammatical; 'turbidity' is a noun used as a verb. Rephrase as a coherent rhetorical question about clarifying turbidity.

issues.span: neighboring states
issues.advice: 畏四鄰 in Daoist context means 'wary of the four neighbors' (surrounding people/neighbors), not necessarily states; avoid political overtones.

payload.translation: Ceux qui savent bien faire des hommes sont subtils, mystérieux, profonds et inconnus. C'est pourquoi, pour les rendre accessibles, on leur donne des apparences douces et confiantes, comme si l'on traversait un fleuve en hiver, comme si l'on craignait les quatre voisins, comme si l'on était un étranger, comme si l'eau se dissolvait, comme si l'on était comme la brique brute, comme si l'on était comme la vallée, comme si l'on était comme la boue. Qui peut rendre la clarté par le silence ? Qui peut calmer la turbulence par la patience ? Le vieillard garde cette voie sans vouloir être plein. C'est parce qu'il ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé sans jamais être nouveau.

issues.span: Ceux qui savent bien faire des hommes
issues.advice: The source 善為士者 means 'those who were skilled as masters/scholars (士)', not 'those who know how to make men'. Translate 士 as 'masters' or 'scholars' and 為 as 'being/acting as', not 'faire des hommes'.

issues.span: pour les rendre accessibles, on leur donne des apparences
issues.advice: The source 故彊為之容 means 'therefore one is forced to describe their appearance/features' (彊 = forced/reluctantly, 容 = appearance). It does not mean 'to make them accessible, one gives them appearances'.

issues.span: comme si l'on était comme la brique brute
issues.advice: 敦兮其若樸: 樸 means 'uncarved wood/block', not 'brique brute' (raw brick). Use 'bois non dégrossi' or 'simplicité du bois brut'.

issues.span: comme si l'on était comme la boue
issues.advice: 渾兮其若濁 means 'chaotic/murky like turbid water', not 'like mud'. Use 'trouble' or 'eau trouble'.

issues.span: Qui peut rendre la clarté par le silence ? Qui peut calmer la turbulence par la patience ?
issues.advice: The source 孰能濁以靜之徐清孰能安以乆動之徐生 means 'Who can, being turbid, quiet it and gradually clarify? Who can, being at rest, through long movement gradually generate life?' The translation reverses the logic and omits 徐生 (gradual generation).

issues.span: Le vieillard garde cette voie
issues.advice: 保此道者 means 'those who preserve this Way', not specifically 'the old man' (vieillard). Use 'celui qui garde cette voie'.

issues.span: qu'il peut être épuisé sans jamais être nouveau
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'therefore he can be worn out without needing new completion/without being newly made' — i.e., he can endure decay without renewal. The translation 'épuisé sans jamais être nouveau' misses 新成 (newly completed/made new).

issues.span: 彊為之容
issues.advice: 彊 (qiǎng) here means 'forced/constrained', rendered as 'on est contraint de décrire son apparence', not 'pour les rendre accessibles'.

issues.span: comme si l'on était comme la brique brute, comme si l'on était comme la vallée, comme si l'on était comme la boue
issues.advice: Repetitive 'comme si l'on était comme' is awkward; vary with 'tel le bois brut', 'tel le val', 'tel l'eau trouble'.

payload.translation: Celui qui sait bien agir comme un maître ou un savant est subtil, mystérieux, profond et inconnu. C'est pourquoi il est contraint de se mettre en apparence douce et confiante, tel qu'on traverse un fleuve en hiver, tel qu'on craignait les quatre voisins, tel qu'on était un étranger, tel que l'eau se dissolvait, tel le bois non dégrossi, tel la vallée, tel l'eau trouble. Qui peut rendre la clarté par le silence ? Qui peut calmer la turbulence par la patience ? Celui qui garde cette voie ne veut pas être plein. C'est parce qu'il ne veut pas être plein qu'il peut être épuisé sans jamais être renouvelé.

issues.span: Celui qui sait bien agir comme un maître ou un savant
issues.advice: The source 善為士者 means 'those who were skilled as masters/scholars' in antiquity; the rendering splits 士 into 'maître ou un savant' and adds 'savoir bien agir', distorting the sense. Render as 'Ceux qui, dans l'Antiquité, excellaient comme maîtres...'.

issues.span: C'est pourquoi il est contraint de se mettre en apparence douce et confiante
issues.advice: 彊為之容 means 'one is forced to describe/outline their appearance', not that the person puts on a gentle appearance. The subject of 彊為 is the speaker, not the master.

issues.span: tel qu'on craignait les quatre voisins
issues.advice: 猶若畏四鄰 means 'hesitant as if fearing the four neighbors' — a description of the master's cautious demeanor, not a past fear by 'on'. Use 'hésitant comme celui qui craint ses quatre voisins'.

issues.span: tel que l'eau se dissolvait
issues.advice: 渙若冰將釋 means 'dissolving like ice about to melt' — the simile describes the person, not water dissolving. Use 'se dissolvant comme la glace sur le point de fondre'.

issues.span: Qui peut rendre la clarté par le silence ? Qui peut calmer la turbulence par la patience ?
issues.advice: 孰能濁以靜之徐清 / 孰能安以乆動之徐生 means 'Who can, from turbidity, by stillness, gradually become clear? Who can, from stability, by prolonged movement, gradually come to life?' The translation reverses the causal structure and drops 乆動之徐生.

issues.span: qu'il peut être épuisé sans jamais être renouvelé
issues.advice: 故能弊不新成 means 'thus can be worn out without needing to be newly completed/made new' — i.e., can endure decay without renewal. 'sans jamais être renouvelé' adds 'jamais' and misreads 新成 as 'renouvelé'.

issues.span: la voie
issues.advice: 道 in this context is the Dao; capitalize as 'la Voie' to match standard Daoist terminology.

issues.span: tel qu'on traversait un fleuve en hiver, tel qu'on craignait les quatre voisins, tel qu'on était un étranger, tel que l'eau se dissolvait, tel le bois non dégrossi, tel la vallée, tel l'eau trouble
issues.advice: The repetitive 'tel que/tel' chain is awkward and mixes clauses with nouns; harmonize with 'comme' + noun phrases or 'ainsi que'.

payload.translation: 古に優れた士の人は微妙玄通深不可知である。そのようにして認識できないからこそ、強いてその容姿を豊かにし、安らぎとしよう。冬に川を渡るように、四隣を畏れ、客を待たし、氷が解けるように、朴（くろ）をなぞる。広大であるがゆえに谷のように、混濁であるがゆえに濁りない。誰が静かにして濁り、徐々にして清らかにする。誰が動かし、徐々にして安らぎに保つ。この道に優れた者は、盈（ふん）を求めない。なぜなら、不盈であるからこそ、弊（ひ）を成し、新（しん）を成すことができる。

issues.span: 強いてその容姿を豊かにし、安らぎとしよう
issues.advice: 「彊為之容」は「しいてその姿を形容する」の意。原文の「豫若冬渉川」以下の比喩の列挙を「豊かにし、安らぎとしよう」と誤って接続している。

issues.span: 客を待たし
issues.advice: 「儼若客」は「客のように謹厳である」の意で、「客を待つ」ではない。

issues.span: 朴（くろ）をなぞる
issues.advice: 「敦兮其若樸」は「厚くして素朴なこと、あたかも未加工の木のよう」の意。「なぞる」は誤り、また「朴」の読み「くろ」は不適切。

issues.span: 混濁であるがゆえに濁りない
issues.advice: 「渾兮其若濁」は「混じり合って濁っているようである」の意。「濁りない」は原文と逆。

issues.span: 誰が静かにして濁り、徐々にして清らかにする
issues.advice: 「孰能濁以靜之徐清」は「濁ったものを静めて徐々に清くできるのは誰か」の意。主客が逆転している。

issues.span: 誰が動かし、徐々にして安らぎに保つ
issues.advice: 「孰能安以乆動之徐生」は「安らかなものを久しく動かして徐々に生かすのは誰か」の意。意味が取れていない。

issues.span: 弊（ひ）を成し、新（しん）を成すことができる
issues.advice: 「故能弊不新成」は「だからこそ古びて新たに成ることはない（壊れても新しく作り直す必要がない）」の意。「弊を成し新を成す」は誤訳。

issues.span: 盈（ふん）
issues.advice: 「盈」の読みは「えい」。「ふん」は誤り。

issues.span: 安らぎとしよう
issues.advice: 原文の比喩列挙と接続しない不自然な文。文脈に合わせて「しいて形容すれば」と導くべき。

issues.span: 朴（くろ）
issues.advice: 「樸」は「ぼく」または「あらき」と読み、「未加工の木」の意。「くろ」は当て字の誤り。

payload.translation: 古に優れた士は微妙玄通深不可知なり。そのようにして認識できないからこそ、強いてその容姿を豊かにし、安らぎとしよう。冬に川を渡るように、四隣を畏れ、客を待たし、氷が解けるように、朴（くろ）をなぞる。広大であるがゆえに谷のように、混濁であるがゆえに濁りない。誰が静かにして濁りを除き、徐々に清らかにする。誰が動かし、徐々に安らぎに保つ。この道に優れた者は、盈（えい）を求めない。なぜなら、不盈であるからこそ、弊（ひ）を成し、新（しん）を成すことができる。

issues.span: 強いてその容姿を豊かにし、安らぎとしよう
issues.advice: 原文「彊為之容」は「しいて（その姿を）形容する」の意。「豊かにし、安らぎとしよう」は意味の付加・誤訳。

issues.span: 客を待たし
issues.advice: 「儼若客」は「客のように謹厳である」の意。「客を待たし」は主客転倒の誤訳。

issues.span: 朴（くろ）をなぞる
issues.advice: 「敦兮其若樸」は「厚朴として未加工の木のよう」の意。「なぞる」は誤り、また「朴」の読み「くろ」は不適切。

issues.span: 混濁であるがゆえに濁りない
issues.advice: 「渾兮其若濁」は「混然として濁っているよう」の意。「濁りない」は正反対の誤訳。

issues.span: 誰が静かにして濁りを除き、徐々に清らかにする
issues.advice: 「孰能濁以靜之徐清」は「濁りを静めて徐々に清くできるのは誰か」の意。訳文は疑問の構文が崩れ、主語・目的語関係が不明瞭。

issues.span: 誰が動かし、徐々に安らぎに保つ
issues.advice: 「孰能安以乆動之徐生」は「安きを久しくして動かし徐々に生ぜしめる」の意。「安らぎに保つ」は「生」の訳抜け・意味の誤り。

issues.span: 弊（ひ）を成し、新（しん）を成すことができる
issues.advice: 「能弊不新成」は「古びて新たに成らない（新成を求めない）」の意。「弊を成し新を成す」は正反対の誤訳。

issues.span: 盈（えい）
issues.advice: 「盈」に「えい」とルビを振るのは日本語の訓みとして不自然。老子の用語として「盈（み）つ」等、文脈に即した扱いにすべき。

issues.span: 冬に川を渡るように、四隣を畏れ、客を待たし、氷が解けるように
issues.advice: 「豫若」「猶若」「儼若」「渙若」の並列比喩の構造が崩れ、日本語としても不自然。各句を「〜のようだ」で統一すべき。

issues.span: 朴（くろ）
issues.advice: 「樸」は「ぼく」または「あらき」と訓むのが通例で、「くろ」は誤った訓。

payload.translation: I am writing a biography of Ah Q, and it has been more than two years. Yet, while I am writing, I am constantly recalling the past, which shows that I am not a man of 'establishing a legacy.' For an immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man; thus, people write to immortalize, and the immortalized person writes to be immortalized. Ultimately, it is unclear who is writing for whom, and finally, it all comes down to writing about Ah Q, as if there were ghosts in my thoughts.

issues.span: it has been more than two years
issues.advice: The source says '已经不止一两年了' meaning 'more than one or two years' (i.e., several years), not specifically 'more than two years'; render as 'more than a year or two' or 'for several years now'.

issues.span: while I am writing, I am constantly recalling the past
issues.advice: '一面要做，一面又往回想' means while intending to write, I keep having second thoughts / keep turning it over in my mind—not 'recalling the past'; revise to convey hesitation/reconsideration.

issues.span: a man of 'establishing a legacy'
issues.advice: '立言' is a classical Confucian concept (establishing words/teachings that endure), conventionally rendered 'establishing one's words' or 'leaving words for posterity'; 'establishing a legacy' loses the allusion.

issues.span: people write to immortalize, and the immortalized person writes to be immortalized
issues.advice: The source '人以文传，文以人传' means 'the man is transmitted through his writing, and the writing is transmitted through the man'—a mutual transmission, not 'people write to immortalize'; revise to reflect mutual dependence of person and text.

issues.span: who is writing for whom
issues.advice: '究竟谁靠谁传' means 'who relies on whom to be transmitted/handed down', not 'who is writing for whom'; correct the sense of reliance/transmission.

issues.span: as if there were ghosts in my thoughts
issues.advice: '仿佛思想里有鬼似的' idiomatically means 'as if something were haunting my mind' or 'as if a ghost were in my thoughts'; the current phrasing is awkward.

payload.translation: I have been writing a biography of Ah Q for several years now. Yet, while I am in the process of writing, I am constantly turning it over in my mind; this shows that I am not a man of 'establishing words.' An immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man; thus, people write to immortalize, and the immortalized person writes to be immortalized. Ultimately, it is unclear who relies on whom to be transmitted, and finally, it all comes down to writing about Ah Q, as if there were ghosts in my thoughts.

issues.span: I have been writing a biography of Ah Q for several years now
issues.advice: The source says '已经不止一两年了' (more than a year or two), not 'several years'; also '我要给阿Q做正传' expresses intent/plan, not completed ongoing action. Render as 'It has been more than a year or two that I have wanted to write the true story of Ah Q.'

issues.span: a biography
issues.advice: '正传' is a specific term (the 'true story' / orthodox biography), not a generic 'biography'; preserve the ironic title term.

issues.span: a man of 'establishing words'
issues.advice: '立言' is a classical Confucian concept (establishing words that endure); a literal gloss loses the allusion. Consider 'a man who establishes words' with awareness of the classical reference.

issues.span: people write to immortalize, and the immortalized person writes to be immortalized
issues.advice: The source '人以文传，文以人传' means 'the man is transmitted through the writing, and the writing is transmitted through the man' — i.e., mutual transmission, not 'writes to be immortalized.' Correct the direction of the relation.

issues.span: who relies on whom to be transmitted
issues.advice: '谁靠谁传' refers to who depends on whom for transmission/handling down, not 'to be transmitted' passively; render as 'who relies on whom to be handed down.'

issues.span: as if there were ghosts in my thoughts
issues.advice: '仿佛思想里有鬼似的' idiomatically means 'as if something were haunting my thoughts' / 'as if a ghost were in my head'; the plural 'ghosts' and 'thoughts' is awkward.

issues.span: An immortal pen must be used to immortalize a man
issues.advice: '不朽之笔，须传不朽之人' is a classical aphorism; the translation flattens it into a generic statement. Preserve the aphoristic, slightly archaic register.

payload.translation: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat vague; even his former deeds are vague. For the people of Weizhuang, as to Aq, as long as he helps them, they only take him for a joke, and never pay attention to his deeds. And Aq himself does not say so, but only when he has a quarrel with others, he sometimes squints his eyes and says: "We were once much more superior to you! What sort of thing are you?"

issues.span: Aq is not only his name and place of origin somewhat vague
issues.advice: The opening is garbled; the subject 'his name and place of origin' should be the thing that is vague, not Aq himself. Restructure so it reads that not only are his name and native place vague.

issues.span: Weizhuang
issues.advice: The village name is conventionally rendered 'Weizhuang' but the standard Lu Xun translation uses 'Wei Village' or 'Weichuang'; pick a consistent established rendering.

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they only take him for a joke
issues.advice: The source means they only want him to help and only make fun of him; 'take him for a joke' misreads 拿他玩笑 (make fun of him). Render as 'they only made fun of him'.

issues.span: And Aq himself does not say so
issues.advice: The source says Aq himself did not talk about it (his 行状/deeds), not 'does not say so'; clarify the referent.

issues.span: squints his eyes
issues.advice: 瞪着眼睛 means to glare or stare wide-eyed, not squint; correct to 'glare' or 'stare'.

issues.span: We were once much more superior to you
issues.advice: 我们先前——比你阔的多啦 means 'we were once much richer/more prosperous than you'; 'superior' loses the 阔 (wealthy) sense. Use 'much richer than you'.

issues.span: For the people of Weizhuang, as to Aq, as long as he helps them, they only take him for a joke
issues.advice: The clause chain is awkward and ungrammatical; smooth the syntax so the sentence flows naturally in English.

payload.translation: Aq's name and place of origin are vague, and so are his former deeds. For the people of Weizhuang, as long as he helps them, they only make fun of him; they never pay attention to his deeds. Aq himself does not say so, but only when he has a quarrel with others does he sometimes glare and say, "We were once much richer than you! What sort of thing are you?"

issues.span: Aq himself does not say so
issues.advice: The source 而阿Q自己也不说 means Aq himself does not talk about his 行状/deeds; 'does not say so' wrongly implies he does not say the preceding statement. Render as 'Aq himself did not talk about it either' or similar.

issues.span: deeds
issues.advice: 『行状』 is a quasi-official term for a biographical account/record of conduct; 'deeds' loses the mock-formal register. Consider 'biographical record' or 'record of conduct' (perhaps in quotes) to preserve the ironic tone.

issues.span: Weizhuang
issues.advice: 未庄 is conventionally rendered 'Weizhuang' but often as 'Wei Village' or 'the village of Wei'; ensure consistency with established translation conventions for this text.

issues.span: We were once much richer than you
issues.advice: The source 我们先前——比你阔的多啦 uses 我们 (we/our family) which is fine, but 'much richer' should reflect 阔的多啦 more idiomatically as 'far richer' or 'much better off'; minor.

issues.span: as long as he helps them, they only make fun of him
issues.advice: The clause structure is slightly awkward; the source means they only want his help and only make fun of him, never noting his record. Rephrase for smoother logic, e.g. 'they only wanted his help and only made fun of him'.
